author: swain
title: Keep meeting schedules tied to the requested body
body: An official county page can publish a valid recurring schedule for the wrong body. The live judge reproduced this when the schedule agent returned the county board’s meetings for a sheriff’s office. When sources do not establish a recurrence for the requested body, returning no schedule is safer than sending an official to someone else’s meeting or storing the wrong page for future runs.

@@ -206,6 +206,7 @@ In dev/QA, `meetingBriefingsDaily` will fan out one job per onboarded `ElectedOf
 
 ## Gotchas
 
+- **A schedule belongs to the body that holds it.** The prompt's Step 2b requires positive evidence that the body `office` names is the one meeting, because runs on `a3-below_threshold` twice answered a county sheriff with the county board of commissioners' schedule — an easy, adjacent, wrong answer on the same county site. `status: "found"` naming a different body than the office is a wrong answer, not a thin one, and the fix is `not_found` with the trail in `sources`. Do not fix a case like it by naming the office title in the prompt: a title that reads like one officer is sometimes a body (`"Commissioners Court"`), and the same failure returns on the next single-officeholder seat. `meetingSchedule.prompt.test.ts` holds the rule to both directions — never substitute another body, and never read a rename (`"Common Council"` for `"City Council"`) as a different one.
 - **`onElectedOfficeCreated` auto-dispatches a schedule experiment** when `MEETINGS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED=true`. Toggling this on in dev caused noise during initial rollout; default to off outside prod.
 - **Internal data source names must not leak.** Tables like `int__l2_nationwide_uniform_w_haystaq` and any column starting with `hs_` / `l2_` are internal. The `DISTRICT_INSIGHTS_RULES` block enforces this on the chat path, but the briefing artifact itself can still embed these names — the frontend (and any future export path) must mask at the boundary.
 - **`AnnotationNote.body` is nullable.** Anything reading notes for AI context, surface display, or search must consider the attachment OCR fallback. The current `BriefingNotesService.loadNotesForChat` filters notes with empty body — confirm whether that's intentional for your call site (see "Notes, dictation, and transcription" above). **TODO: verify** that the recent context-unification work actually wires OCR text into this path.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/gp-api/src/meetings/meetingScheduleAgent/meetingSchedule.prompt.test.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { MEETING_SCHEDULE_PROMPT } from './meetingSchedule.prompt'
+import { MeetingScheduleOutputSchema } from './meetingSchedule.schema'
+
+// The model copies the prompt's examples and its RRULE table, so an example the
+// agent's own schema rejects costs every run that follows it: `submitOutput`
+// refuses the artifact and the run spends its turns fixing a sample the prompt
+// wrote wrong.
+const examples = () =>
+  [...MEETING_SCHEDULE_PROMPT.matchAll(/```json\n([\s\S]*?)```/g)].map(
+    (match) => JSON.parse(match[1]!) as { status: string },
+  )
+
+// Only the reference table, which is the block the model is told to copy. Bare
+// fragments elsewhere in the prompt (`FREQ=`, `DTSTART`) are prose about the
+// field, not samples. Each row is `| plain English | RRULE |`, so the second
+// column is taken whole: matching on a `FREQ=` prefix instead would let a
+// mistyped row drop out of the check silently rather than fail it.
+const rrules = () =>
+  [
+    ...MEETING_SCHEDULE_PROMPT.matchAll(/^\s*\|[^|]+\|\s*`([^`]+)`\s*\|\s*$/gm),
+  ].map((match) => match[1]!)
+
+const foundArtifact = (rrule: string) => ({
+  generated_at: '2026-11-23T00:00:00Z',
+  status: 'found',
+  meeting_name: 'City Council',
+  location: 'City Hall Council Chambers, 200 Main St',
+  rrule,
+  human: 'Second and fourth Monday of every month',
+  time: '19:00',
+  timezone: 'America/Chicago',
+  duration_minutes: 120,
+  sources: [{ url: 'https://example.gov/agendas', note: 'states it' }],
+  discovered_schedule_location: null,
+})
+
+describe('meeting_schedule prompt', () => {
+  it('carries a found example and a not_found example', () => {
+    expect(
+      examples()
+        .map((example) => example.status)
+        .sort(),
+    ).toEqual(['found', 'not_found'])
+  })
+
+  it('writes every example in the shape the agent validates', () => {
+    for (const example of examples()) {
+      expect(() => MeetingScheduleOutputSchema.parse(example)).not.toThrow()
+    }
+  })
+
+  it('writes every RRULE in the reference table so the schema accepts it', () => {
+    expect(rrules()).toHaveLength(7)
+    for (const rrule of rrules()) {
+      expect(rrule).toContain('FREQ=')
+      expect(rrule).not.toContain('DTSTART')
+      expect(
+        MeetingScheduleOutputSchema.safeParse(foundArtifact(rrule)).success,
+      ).toBe(true)
+    }
+  })
+
+  // a3-below_threshold: two attempts answered a county sheriff with the county
+  // board of commissioners' schedule. The rule those runs missed is that the
+  // schedule has to belong to the office's own body, and it has to hold in both
+  // directions so the prompt cannot drift into refusing a body the source calls
+  // by another name, or into reading a shared building as a shared body.
+  it('requires the schedule to belong to the office’s own body', () => {
+    const section =
+      MEETING_SCHEDULE_PROMPT.split('### Step 2b')[1]!.split('### Step 3')[0]!
+    expect(section).toContain('same body, same jurisdiction')
+    expect(section).toContain('Never substitute another body')
+    expect(section).toContain('A renamed body is the same body')
+    expect(section).toContain('A shared room cuts both ways')
+  })
+
+  // The fix is general: the office's own page and code decide whether it meets,
+  // never a title the prompt blacklists. Naming one makes the same failure come
+  // back on the next single-officeholder seat.
+  it('does not key the rule to one office title', () => {
+    expect(MEETING_SCHEDULE_PROMPT).not.toMatch(/sheriff/i)
+  })
+})
